subject: Private deployment orchestration — Terraform / Helm / Ansible convergence check-in
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tomas Berg <tomas@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T16:12:00Z
Subject: Kickoff: convergence of TF / Helm / Ansible for ApexHealth private deploy

Hi team,

Thanks for the quick intake call earlier. To summarize, ApexHealth is asking us to consolidate three separate deliverables into a single gated delivery for their private VPC deployment:

- Terraform modules for network, subnets, and route tables (multi-AZ)
- Helm charts for the runtime services (ingress, load-balancer, sidecars)
- Ansible playbooks for host-level config and bootstrap (mtls certs, monitoring agents)

Primary concerns they called out: IP range overlap with their on-prem carveout, a strict pre-prod mirroring requirement (everything staged identical to prod), and audit evidence for CI gating (who approved what + artifact hashes).

Action items I want us to cover in the first review:
1) CI gating: pre-merge plan + policy to prevent drift (who owns the policy?)
2) Network checklist: explicit IP allocation table and NAT/bastion constraints
3) Helm values & secrets flow: how do we avoid leaking KMS keys into pipeline logs
4) Upgrade/fallback policy: how rollbacks are coordinated between TF and Helm

I'm attaching the initial ApexHealth environment worksheet they sent (infra-team@apexhealth.com). Can we set a working session next week to walk the Terraform plan + proposed Helm values?

Attachments: apex_infra_workbook.xlsx (stub)

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tomas Berg <tomas@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: convergence of TF / Helm / Ansible for ApexHealth private deploy

Thanks Aditya — good summary.

Quick notes after a first pass on their workbook:
- IPs: they have an RFC1918 carveout that overlaps our staging VPC ranges in one AZ. We need a nonbreaking remap plan (suggestion: reserve a /22 per AZ for ApexHealth and run a NAT GW per AZ).
- CI gating: we should leverage the existing INFRA pipeline but add a \"policy check\" job that fails on non-authorized changes to tfstate-affecting modules. I'll propose INFRA-239 in Jira for the policy job.
- Drift detection: add a nightly plan compare (terraform plan -detailed-exitcode) and push artifacts to the audit bucket with build metadata.
- Helm/Secrets: recommend a sealed-secrets flow that uploads sealed payloads to the release pipeline; decryption only happens at deploy time in customer env where KMS is present. Avoid storing plaintext in the pipeline.

I've dropped an updated network diagram into Drive (network-diagram-v2.png) with suggested carveouts and a short legend. Please review before the sync.

Proposed working session: 2026-08-05 15:00 PT (60m) — please confirm availability.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Tomas Berg <tomas@apexhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T11:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: convergence of TF / Helm / Ansible for ApexHealth private deploy

Agree with Marissa. A couple of concrete CI suggestions:
- Add a pre-merge gate that runs: terraform validate -> terraform plan (compare to last approved plan) -> helm lint + helm dry-run against a local k3s cluster.
- Enforce signed commits for module owners and require two approvers for changes that touch networking modules.
- Add a canary rollout flag in Helm values to allow traffic shaping during first 12 hours.

I'll create the pipeline snippets and attach to INFRA-239. Also happy to lead the canary rollout playbook.

-Lauren
Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Tomas Berg <tomas@apexhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T01:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: convergence of TF / Helm / Ansible for ApexHealth private deploy

Appreciate the fast turn. A few clarifications from our infra/security team:
- We cannot accept a NAT-only design; on-prem VPN peers will require static routes. Can you provide the exact /24 assignments you propose per AZ? We prefer explicitness in the contract.
- Audit evidence: we need signed artifacts (hash + approver) preserved for 365 days. Is that compatible with Redwood's audit bucket retention?
- Secrets: our security team will only permit sealed-secrets if the public key is generated and rotated on our KMS. We will provide credentials for testing in a staging account.

Can we aim to have the detailed IP table and CI gating checklist before the 08/05 meeting?

Thanks,
Tomas
Head of Cloud Engineering
ApexHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tomas Berg <tomas@apexhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: convergence of TF / Helm / Ansible for ApexHealth private deploy — action items & materials

Folks — following up with consolidated deliverables ahead of today's session.

Deliverables attached: terraform-diff.patch (high level diffs for the proposed network carve), values-prod.yaml (helm candidate values for canary), network-diagram-v2.png (already in Drive).

Consolidated action items:
1) Aditya: finalize the /24 per-AZ table and send to Tomas by EOD 08/06.
2) Lauren: create the INFRA-239 pipeline snippets (pre-merge policy + plan-compare job). Target: 08/07 PR.
3) Olga: draft the rollback coordination runbook (how TF/Helm rollback interplay). Target: 08/09.
4) Marissa (me): confirm audit retention with infra and circulate the signed-artifact storage spec (I'll coordinate with Security).

I captured the DocuSign reference Tomas mentioned (we'll need it for the network carve confirmation) — share once countersigned.

If anyone sees a missing piece, flag it here. Otherwise we'll use today's meeting to walk the tf plan and Helm values and capture live feedback.

Attachments: terraform-diff.patch (stub), values-prod.yaml (stub)

Regards,
